hypothesis: If marine forms change almost simultaneously worldwide, then the stratigraphic-stage boundaries of marine genus turnover in the PBDB occur in the same time bins on every ocean basin/continent, so regional extinction/origination peaks coincide with global ones.
pass_criterion: Using marine-invertebrate genus occurrences from PBDB (Phanerozoic, stage-level bins), compute per-bin origination and extinction rates separately for at least 4 paleocontinental/regional subsets (e.g., North America, Europe, Asia, Australia/Gondwana). Claim passes if the mean pairwise Spearman rank correlation of regional per-bin turnover rates is >= 0.5 (p<0.01) and at least 70% of the global top-10 turnover bins are also in the top 20% of turnover bins in each region.
fail_criterion: Claim fails if the mean pairwise Spearman correlation of regional per-bin turnover rates is < 0.3 or if fewer than 40% of global top-10 turnover bins fall in the top 20% of bins in the regional subsets, indicating regionally asynchronous change.
interpretation: Darwin's 'forms of life' = marine fossil genera/species; 'change' = origination and extinction (faunal turnover) between successive stratigraphic intervals; 'almost simultaneously in a broad geological sense' = within the same stage-length time bin (~10 Myr scale), not instantaneous. 'Throughout the world' = across separate regions with different paleolatitudes/climates. Modern reinterpretation: correlation is tested through numeric ages (time bins) of occurrences in PBDB rather than by fossil-based correlation itself, avoiding circularity by using binned absolute ages and regional comparison of turnover rates. Sampling bias is addressed by using rarefied or range-through rates.

dataset.name: The Paleobiology Database
dataset.why_it_fits: PBDB holds global marine fossil occurrences with taxonomic identification, geographic coordinates/paleocoordinates, country/continent and numeric early/late ages (max_ma, min_ma) via the data1.2 API and download generator. Fields used: accepted_name, genus, early_interval, max_ma, min_ma, cc (country), lng/lat, paleolng/paleolat, environment (marine). These allow computing regional per-bin turnover and comparing across regions.
